name: SVT-AV1
summary: SVT-AV1 is the Alliance for Open Media's production AV1 encoder (Scalable Video Technology, originally from Intel and Netflix). Its strengths are good multi-core scaling, a very wide preset range from research-slow to real-time, solid efficiency around presets 2-6, and built-in film-grain synthesis plus perceptual tools ported from the community PSY forks (variance boost, AC bias, sharpness, IQ tune). Its weaknesses: the installed build only encodes 4:2:0 at 8 or 10 bits, it never places keyframes at scene cuts, it has no HDR10+ or Dolby Vision options in the stand-alone CLI, and the many forks and fast-moving defaults make guides go stale quickly.
license: BSD 3-Clause Clear License plus the Alliance for Open Media Patent License 1.0

hdr.summary: Feed a 10-bit Y4M (or raw YUV with --input-depth 10) that is already PQ or HLG encoded; SVT-AV1 does not convert transfer functions or bit depth. Signal the color description with --color-primaries 9 (bt2020), --transfer-characteristics 16 (smpte2084, HDR10/PQ) or 18 (hlg), --matrix-coefficients 9 (bt2020-ncl) and --color-range 0 (studio). For HDR10, add static metadata with --mastering-display 'G(x,y)B(x,y)R(x,y)WP(x,y)L(max,min)' where the luminance values are plain nits (floats), and --content-light MaxCLL,MaxFALL as integers. --chroma-sample-position topleft (colocated) follows the official HDR example and the usual siting of BT.2020 UHD masters. HLG normally needs only the color description. The stand-alone CLI has no HDR10+ or Dolby Vision input; FFmpeg's libsvtav1 wrapper can pass through Dolby Vision RPUs (-dolbyvision) and copies mastering/CLL side data when it is present on the input stream.
pitfalls: Luminance values in --mastering-display are nits as decimals (L(1000,0.0001)), not the 0.0001-cd/m2 integer units x265 uses; primaries are written G, B, R, then white point.

--input-depth only accepts 8 or 10 and describes the input file as well as the output; an 8-bit pipe cannot become a real HDR encode, and there is no 12-bit or 4:2:2/4:4:4 support in this build (use libaom for those).
--luminance-qp-bias assumes a gamma-like signal; the Codec Wiki parameter study says to use it only on SDR and HLG, not on PQ (HDR10) material.
Mainline variance boost curves are not PQ-aware; the PQ-tuned curve (--variance-boost-curve 3) exists only in the svt-av1-hdr fork, so do not copy fork command lines into mainline.

The IVF output carries the color description in the AV1 sequence header and HDR10 static metadata in metadata OBUs; when remuxing, check that the container also gets matching color tags, since some muxers do not derive them from the bitstream.
--content-light 0,0 means unknown; supply real MaxCLL/MaxFALL when you have measured them.
No --hdr10plus-json or --dolby-vision-rpu in the installed mainline CLI (those are svt-av1-hdr fork options); dynamic metadata must be handled by FFmpeg (-dolbyvision) or added at mux time.
FFmpeg's -crf for libsvtav1 is an integer 0-63; fractional or >63 CRF needs -svtav1-params crf=..., and -svtav1-params is parsed last so it overrides FFmpeg-level color fields.
HDR sources are often 4K or larger: v4.3.0 caps random-access encodes at preset 9 at 4K and above, and rejects presets 4 and below above 4K (for example 8K).

presets.speed: Slowest (research mode, MR); somewhat slower than preset 0
presets.notes: Reference point in the Codec Wiki v3.0 study; preset 0 averaged only about 1% worse BD-rate. In v1.8 tests preset 4 was about 50-60x faster than -1. The help calls negative presets debugging presets. Not worth it for real encodes.

presets.speed: Extremely slow; about 5-10x slower than preset 4 in v1.8 tests
presets.notes: About 0.97% worse than -1 (v3.0, average of SSIMULACRA2/Butteraugli/XPSNR/W-VMAF). Codec Wiki v2.2 tests advised against spending time on 0 and -1 except at extremely low quality targets; Streaming Learning Center suggests it only for files with millions of views.

presets.speed: Very slow; roughly 2x slower than preset 2
presets.notes: About 3.79% worse than -1 in v3.0 tests; only a narrow gain over preset 2.

presets.speed: Slow; slightly more than 2x faster than preset 1 and about 2x slower than preset 3
presets.notes: About 7.82% worse than -1, i.e. close to preset 1. Codec Wiki calls presets 2 and 4 the best value for the time spent among the slower presets.

presets.speed: Slow; about 1.5x faster than preset 2 (v2.2 tests)
presets.notes: About 17.08% worse than -1 in v3.0; there is a large efficiency step between 2 and 3, and preset 4 is close behind 3.

presets.speed: Moderate; roughly 2x faster than preset 2 in v1.8 tests; there is a large speed jump from 4 to 5
presets.notes: About 22.41% worse than -1 in v3.0, but very close to preset 3. Widely used as the balance point (Codec Wiki deep dives; Streaming Learning Center measured 98.92% of the best VMAF at 3.5% of the encode time on v1.4). Lumora's default. Above 4K (for example 8K), v4.3.0 rejects presets 4 and below for video encodes (all-intra excepted) because of memory use.
In v3.0 about 44% faster than in v2.0 but about 4.5% less efficient (worse on gaming clips). Good start of the 'fast but still good' range.

v3.0 about 47% faster than v2.0 at 8.8% lower efficiency. Codec Wiki suggests 6 or 8 if 4 is too slow. Highest preset that does not print the film-grain compute-overhead warning (the warning fires above preset 6 when --film-grain is on).
v3.0 about 68% faster than v2.0 for about 11.6% efficiency loss; preset 8 sometimes matches or beats it.
Codec Wiki considers 8 the last truly usable preset in v3.0 and found it occasionally equal to 6 by W-VMAF. Film grain above preset 6 triggers a compute-overhead warning.
Codec Wiki saw non-monotonic, inconsistent quality at low CRF for 9 and 10. In v4.3.0 random-access encodes at 4K and above are capped to preset 9.
Outside --rtc, v4.3.0 warns that M10 and faster are meant for automation tooling and may show artifacts. Not recommended for quality work.
Speed/testing use only. The v3.0 changelog speaks of a max of M10; the v4.3.0 source clamps random-access presets above 11 to 11, so whether 11 differs from 10 for VOD was not verified.
Mapped to M11 with a warning in random-access mode (v4.3.0 source); distinct only with --rtc.

presets.speed: Same as 11 for VOD; fastest RTC preset
presets.notes: Mapped to M11 in random access; with --rtc it is labeled experimental and meant for speed evaluation.

rateControl.notes: Default and recommended for home/archival use. Equivalent to --rc 0 --aq-mode 2 --qp x. Values above 63 use the extended quarter-step range added in v4.0.
Turns adaptive QP off; useful for experiments and per-frame QP files, less efficient for real encodes.
Quality-targeted encode with a bitrate ceiling, useful for streaming ladders.
The project says extra passes in CRF mainly help corner cases such as high motion; usually not critical.
Targets an average bitrate; less efficient than CRF; rate tolerance via --undershoot-pct/--overshoot-pct.
Best way to hit a file size; --gop-constraint-rc 1 matches rate per GOP when GOP > 119 frames.
Always single pass; for real-time/low-delay streaming. Variance boost is disabled automatically in CBR.

options.description: Shortcut to silence progress printing.
Main speed/efficiency dial. Lower presets enable more coding tools and search harder, giving smaller files at the same quality but much longer encodes.

recommendations.why: Efficiency close to preset 1 at about half its time; Codec Wiki names presets 2 and 4 the best efficiency-for-time choices.
Nearly as efficient as preset 3 and the usual balance point for enthusiasts; presets 4-6 are the project's suggested home range.
Codec Wiki's animation deep dive used and recommended preset 4 as the balance; going to preset 0 cost 5-10x time for about 1.5 SSIMULACRA2 points.
Suggested when preset 4 is too slow; 8 is the last preset Codec Wiki considers fully usable in v3.0.
Streaming Learning Center found 3-6 the useful VOD range on v1.4 and only very popular titles justify preset 0.

options.lumora: '--preset {preset}', default '4'. EncodeRecipes AV1 ladder offers presets 9, 8, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0 (preset 10 dropped: SVT-AV1 warns that non-RTC presets 10+ may show artifacts, and 9 was 23% smaller for 32% more CPU time), then continues into libaom cpu-used 4-0. Speeds are CPU time per frame measured on an M3 Max, relative to preset 10 (the scale the libaom rungs share); film-grain synthesis is offered on presets 6 and slower only. MacOptimizer benchmarks a fast preset to choose the instance count (docs/encoding/tuning-svtav1.md).
options.notes: v4.3.0 source: random-access presets above 11 map to 11; 4K+ random access caps at 9 (so Lumora's preset 10 rung equals preset 9 at 4K); still-image (--avif) caps at 9; --rtc only allows 7-13. Presets were renumbered in v2.3.0 and v3.0.0, so older preset numbers do not translate one-to-one. Film grain above preset 6 prints a compute-overhead warning. Above 4K resolution, presets 4 and below are rejected for video (all-intra excepted).

options.values: colon-separated key=value list using option names without '--'
options.description: Sets any option through one string, the same syntax FFmpeg's -svtav1-params uses. Handy for passing a whole profile through tools.
options.notes: Duplicate keys are not detected, only invalid keys or values. In FFmpeg it is parsed after the wrapper's own fields, so it wins over -crf, -preset and color options. The help says keys follow config-file names, but Parameters.md and the v4.3.0 parser use the CLI names without '--' (for example preset=4:crf=30).

Codec Wiki recommends 10-bit output for efficiency; the project FAQ says it reduces rounding and banding at a small (~5%) size cost. The two sources disagree on whether it saves or costs bits.

options.notes: Disagreement noted: Codec Wiki says 10-bit is more efficient, the SVT-AV1 FAQ describes a ~5% size cost for slightly better fidelity.

options.description: Feeds pictures to the library at a fixed rate to simulate a live source.
options.notes: Testing aid for real-time pipelines.

Computes PSNR and SSIM against the source and prints a summary at the end (and per frame with --stat-file).
options.notes: Unverified: the film grain appendix says the denoised picture replaces the source when grain denoising is on, so reported PSNR/SSIM may be measured against it. The library warns that stat reports slow the encode.

options.values: c, neon, crc32, neon_dotprod, neon_i8mm, sve, sve2, max
options.description: Caps which SIMD instruction sets the encoder may use. The list shown is the Arm set for this Apple-silicon build; x86 builds list SSE/AVX levels instead.
options.notes: Only for debugging or reproducing results across CPUs.

options.description: Level of parallelism, not a thread count. Higher levels create more threads and keep more pictures in flight for speed at the cost of memory; levels 4+ in CRF also process extra mini-GOPs in parallel.

recommendations.value: lower level per instance (e.g. 3-4) with several instances pinned to separate cores
recommendations.why: The docs show running parallel encodes with a modest --lp each; since output is unchanged, chunked parallel instances scale better than one encode on many cores.

options.lumora: '--lp {svt_lp}': EncoderSpec.render derives the level from the cores one instance fills (threads = cpuCores for a single encode, cpuCores / instances for segments and target-quality chunks) with EncodeRecipes.svtParallelism: 1 core -> 1, 2 -> 2, 3-5 -> 3, 6-11 -> 4, 12-23 -> 5, 24+ -> 6, the table the library's automatic level applies to the whole machine. Measured on an M3 Max: level 6 was never faster than 5 and used 6-12% more memory; memory grows with every level (docs/encoding/tuning-svtav1.md).
options.notes: Replaced the old thread-count meaning (--lp as logical processors) in v2.3.0/v3.0.0. Docs mention a --pin option, but it is not in this build's help.

options.description: Selects the rate-control family: quality-targeted, average-bitrate, or constant-bitrate.

recommendations.why: CRF gives the best quality per file size when no bitrate target is needed.

options.notes: Lumora relies on the default (0) and passes --crf.

options.description: Base quantizer. In CQP it is the fixed level; in CRF it is the starting point the rate control works from.
options.notes: --crf and --cqp are the friendlier forms with quarter steps and a range up to 70.

options.description: Constant rate factor: the main quality dial. Lower values mean higher quality and larger files; it implies adaptive QP (aq-mode 2).

recommendations.why: The project notes 2D animation looks good at higher CRF than live action because it is easy to compress.

recommendations.value: raise CRF a little when enabling variance boost
recommendations.why: Variance boost adds bits to flat areas; Codec Wiki suggests compensating with a higher CRF.

The encoder's own IQ and MS-SSIM tunes pick 4 as the floor (v4.3.0 source), a middle ground between 0 and 8.

options.lumora: Per content type (EncodeRecipes.svtQMMin): 8 for anime, CG and low light, 6 for live action and old anime, 4 for heavy grain and fast motion; at least 8 for HDR10 (PQ) exports. 0 lost 3-8% XPSNR BD-rate on every clip (docs/encoding/tuning-svtav1.md).
options.notes: The SVT-AV1 docs say lower levels lower bitrate with slightly worse quality in CRF, more so at low CRF; community tests saw net efficiency gains. Sources disagree on the best floor (0 vs 4); test on your content.

options.description: Flattest luma matrix allowed (15 = flat). The encoder maps each frame's qindex into the min-max range.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki says leave the maximum alone.

options.notes: Added in v3.1.0 from SVT-AV1-PSY.

options.notes: Added in v3.1.0.

options.description: Region-of-interest map that shifts QP per 64x64 block per picture, for steering bits to faces, text or VR viewports.

options.description: Strength of the motion-compensated temporal filter used to build alt-ref frames. Each step down halves the filtering; strong filtering smooths noise and texture.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki found 1 or lower removes keyframe blocking/smoothing issues, gains flatten below 2, and 4 performs very poorly.
Weaker temporal filtering preserves real grain; the PSY-derived forks default to 1.

options.lumora: '--tf-strength 1' ('Gentle temporal filter') for every content type except anime, including heavy grain, old anime and low light: with grain synthesis the encoder sees a denoised picture, and strength 1 was 15-46% smaller than no temporal filter against the noise-free original. Heavy grain and low light without grain synthesis (presets 8 and 9, grain off, or a film-texture table) get '--enable-tf 0' instead, through EncodeRecipes.svtTemporalFilter (docs/encoding/tuning-svtav1.md).
options.notes: In tune 0 the key-frame filter strength is offset too. The fork-only --kf-tf-strength does not exist in mainline. v4.0.1 fixed the default shown in the help.

options.description: Lowers the QP of darker frames in proportion to how dark they are, to fight dark-scene artifacts.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki's BD-rate figures improved most on anime and got worse on live action and gaming clips; the author suggests testing values such as 10, 30 and 50, considers values below 50 safe, and says it is not suited to PQ.
Frame-average luma does not map to perceived darkness the same way on PQ; the study restricts the feature to SDR and HLG.

options.lumora: Optional 'Brighter handling of dark scenes': '--luminance-qp-bias 25', recommended for real life, heavy grain, low light and old anime. Dropped for HDR10 (PQ) exports by EncodeRecipes.svtArgs on every path (Codec Wiki: SDR and HLG only; on Lumora's PQ clips dropping it saved 1.6-1.9% XPSNR BD-rate). Kept for SDR and HLG: removing it there saved XPSNR but cost VMAF (docs/encoding/tuning-svtav1.md).
options.notes: Documented since v3.0.2. The svt-av1-hdr fork has its own PQ-aware variants.

options.description: Biases the deblocking filter and rate-distortion decisions toward a softer (negative) or crisper (positive) result.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki saw consistent small gains or neutral results at +1/+2 and frequent losses at +4 and above.
The animated test clip (Sol Levante) benefited from positive sharpness while gaming clips did not.

options.lumora: Optional 'Sharper fine detail' / 'Crisper line art': '--sharpness 1' (2 for anime), marked visual-only.
options.notes: Tunes 3 and 4 force sharpness 7. The svt-av1-hdr fork defaults to 1.

options.values: 0: single pass, 1: first pass, 2: second pass
options.description: Runs one pass of a manual multi-pass encode, writing (pass 1) or reading (pass 2) the stats file.
options.notes: Pass 2 is only for VBR; both passes need --stats.

options.description: File holding first-pass statistics for multi-pass encoding.
options.notes: Use a unique name per parallel encode to avoid collisions.

options.description: Runs the whole multi-pass sequence in one command.

recommendations.why: Multi-pass mostly matters for hitting a VBR target; in CRF it only helps corner cases such as high motion.

options.notes: CBR is always one pass. The first pass runs at a fast internal preset.

options.values: -2: ~5 s, -1: infinite (CRF only), 0: same as -1, or frames; 's' suffix for seconds
options.description: Maximum distance between key frames. Longer GOPs save bits; shorter ones help seeking and error recovery.

recommendations.why: The FAQ notes home users prefer 5-10 second GOPs; Codec Wiki suggests about 10x the frame rate.
VOD commonly uses ~1 second GOPs for seeking and packet-loss recovery.

options.notes: SVT-AV1 never inserts keyframes at scene cuts; chunk-based tools (or Lumora's segments) supply them. The 's' suffix works in SvtAv1EncApp but not in FFmpeg's -g. svt-av1-hdr's -2 means ~10 s.

options.values: 1: FWD frame (open GOP), 2: KEY frame (closed GOP)
options.description: Whether periodic intra refreshes are full key frames (closed GOP) or forward key frames (open GOP).

effect.quality: open GOP sometimes + at high CRF

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki advises closed GOP because open-GOP support is incomplete.
The animation deep dive saw open GOP tie or win at high CRF and guessed it might help very grainy content, but flagged this as unconfirmed.

options.notes: Forward key frames force --hierarchical-levels 4 (v4.3.0) and are rejected with CBR.

options.description: Scene change detection switch. In v4.3.0 the library forces it back to 0 with a warning; scene changes are handled inside mode decision without new keyframes.

recommendations.value: leave at 0; split by scenes externally
recommendations.why: The project states SVT-AV1 does not insert keyframes at scene changes regardless of this option and suggests chunked encoding instead.

options.notes: Effectively a no-op in the installed version.

options.description: Extra future frames analyzed beyond what the mini-GOP, temporal filter and rate control already need.
options.lumora: Not set. Lumora used to offer '--lookahead 120'; at preset 4 in CRF mode it produced bit-identical output on a 20 s clip, so the option was removed (docs/encoding/tuning-svtav1.md).
options.notes: v4.3.0 fixed nondeterministic output with --lookahead 0.

options.description: Depth of the hierarchical mini-GOP. More layers mean longer mini-GOPs (up to 32 frames) and better compression of static content; fewer layers react faster to motion.
options.notes: Parameters.md lists 0-5 including flat/2-layer modes; the installed help lists 2-5. Codec Wiki's v2.2 test used 4 to get smaller mini-GOPs but did not recommend a value.

options.description: Random access uses future references (best for files); low delay only references past frames for real-time use.
options.notes: Low delay forces tune 0 to 1 and disallows superres and overlays. Docs also list 0 (all intra).

options.description: Real-time communication mode: forces low-delay prediction and fast RTC-tuned settings.
options.notes: Added in v3.1.0; only presets 7-13 are allowed (lower values become 7).

options.values: comma list of '#f' frame numbers or '#.#s' seconds
options.description: Places key frames at given frames or timestamps, for chapter points or manual scene cuts.
options.notes: Supported for CRF from the command line.

options.description: Uses a shorter mini-GOP right after each key frame, so playback can start and seek faster.
options.notes: CRF/CQP only; must not exceed --hierarchical-levels.

options.description: QP offset added for the first GOP before picture QPs are derived, e.g. to make the opening look better.
options.notes: CRF/CQP only; added in v3.0.

options.description: Splits frames into tile rows for parallel decoding. SVT-AV1 does not need tiles for its own threading.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki found tile rows help decoding less than columns and sometimes regress at low quality.

options.notes: Parameters.md lists default 0; the help says it changes per resolution but is 1.

options.description: Splits frames into tile columns so multi-threaded decoders can work in parallel.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki measured large decode-speed gains with negligible efficiency cost in most clips.
The FAQ suggests tiles to help slow software decoders, warning that many tiles can cause visible artifacts.

options.notes: The encoder prints a reminder to consider --fast-decode when tiles are used for decode speed. Tiles are switched off when superres or resize is enabled (v4.3.0 warns). Codec Wiki's v3.0 tests also treat 0 as the default.

options.description: Deblocking loop filter. Level 2 searches filter levels more precisely at extra cost.
options.notes: Level 2 is a PSY-derived addition; its help text was corrected in v4.1.

options.description: Constrained Directional Enhancement Filter: removes ringing around edges, but can smear fine grain.

recommendations.why: The SVT-AV1 psychovisual appendix says this combination can greatly improve retention of real grain and noise.

options.notes: svt-av1-hdr's tune 6 (film grain) also turns CDEF off; that tune is not in mainline.

options.description: Loop restoration (Wiener and self-guided filters), which smooths reconstruction toward the source.
options.notes: Faster presets disable parts of it automatically (Wiener off from preset 9, self-guided off from preset 4 per the FAQ table). That table was compiled at v2.2.0 and may be outdated.

options.description: Motion-field motion vectors: projects motion from reference frames to predict current vectors.
options.notes: Auto enables it on all presets 0-10 per the FAQ feature table. That table was compiled at v2.2.0 and may be outdated.

options.description: Dynamic GOP: changes the hierarchical structure based on content (for example shorter mini-GOPs in high motion).
Restricts tools so the bitstream decodes faster in software; 2 is more aggressive than 1.

effect.quality: - (about 1% BD-rate for level 1, 1-3% for level 2 per changelog)

recommendations.why: The FAQ lists it first among decode-speed tips; Codec Wiki's v3.0 tests measured average decode gains between about -0.6% and +14.7% depending on preset, level and quality, and saw more macroblocking on some sources.

options.notes: Docs mention an experimental level 3 for still images that requires a special build flag; the installed help lists 0-2. Developed with tune 1, with a warning when combined with tune 0.

options.description: Builds temporally filtered alt-ref frames. They improve compression, but the filtering removes noise from those frames, which can soften grain and fine detail. Mode 2 adapts strength per 64x64 block (experimental).

recommendations.why: The animation deep dive found turning TF off can slightly improve efficiency at high quality and speeds things up, depending on the clip.
Recommended by the SVT-AV1 psychovisual appendix for grain retention.

options.lumora: '--enable-tf 0' for anime: in the planner's 'No temporal smoothing' option and the encoders.json anime tune; and for heavy grain and low light when the encoder codes the real grain (no grain synthesis and no Lumora-removed grain), in place of '--tf-strength 1' (docs/encoding/tuning-svtav1.md).
options.notes: Codec Wiki's v3.0 study found TF-off competitive with low --tf-strength but sometimes slightly worse; Minecraft-like content did worse.

options.description: Applies the temporal filter to key frames as well.
options.notes: New in v4.2.0. Forks expose a separate --kf-tf-strength instead.

options.description: Inserts overlay pictures that give the base layer an extra, unfiltered reference.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki saw neither efficiency nor speed benefit.

options.notes: Not allowed in low delay. v4.3.0 fixed nondeterministic output with overlays. v4.3.0 also rejects overlays with multi-pass encoding.

options.values: 0 = VQ, 1 = PSNR, 2 = SSIM, 3 = IQ (Image Quality), 4 = MS_SSIM (MS-SSIM and SSIMULACRA2 optimized), 5 = VMAF
options.description: Chooses what the encoder optimizes for: subjective sharpness (VQ), PSNR, SSIM, still-image quality, MS-SSIM/SSIMULACRA2, or VMAF. IQ and MS-SSIM also override sharpness, variance boost and QM settings.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki's v3.0 parameter study found tune 1 best overall across SSIMULACRA2, XPSNR, Butteraugli and VMAF, with tune 2 sometimes trading wins.
The Codec Wiki encoder page calls tune 0 the safe psychovisual choice and discourages PSNR tuning; the project FAQ says tune 0 often looks sharper. This disagrees with the metric study above.

recommendations.value: 2 at low quality, 1 at high quality
recommendations.why: The animation deep dive found tunes 1 and 2 matched at high quality and tune 2 ahead at low quality; tune 0 kept detail but could ring.
Parameters.md marks IQ as still-image only.

recommendations.value: 5 when VMAF is the delivery metric
recommendations.why: Added in v4.2.0 targeting about 15% VMAF BD-rate gain at a small PSNR cost. The encoder warns that it applies unsharp-mask pre-processing, so higher VMAF may not mean higher fidelity.

options.lumora: '--tune 0' for anime, both in the planner ('Tune for visual quality', measured -1.1% VMAF and -2.0% XPSNR BD-rate) and in the encoders.json anime tune; every other kind keeps the default (1). Tunes 2 and 4 were larger on Lumora's clips (docs/encoding/tuning-svtav1.md).
options.notes: Tune numbers differ between projects: SVT-AV1-PSY's tune 3 was 'subjective SSIM', mainline's tune 3 is IQ; svt-av1-hdr adds tune 6 (film grain). Low delay forces tune 0 to 1. Tune 5 (VMAF) arrived in v4.2.0; tune 4 (MS-SSIM) is also post-v4.0, but the changelog does not name its release. v4.3.0 validation: tunes 2-5 accept only CRF (--rc 0); tune 3 (IQ) is rejected with random access, so it is for --avif/all-intra (low delay is experimental); tunes 2 and 4 reject low delay; tune 5 needs random access.

options.values: 0: off, 1: on, 2: content adaptive, 3: content adaptive (anti-alias aware)
options.description: Screen-content mode: enables palette and intra block copy tools for text, UI and graphics, either always (1) or when detection says so (2, 3).

recommendations.why: Mode 1 forces block copy and palette tools on; modes 2 and 3 detect it per content.

options.lumora: '--scm 1' for the screen-content kind (encoders.json screen tune and EncodeRecipes 'Screen-content tools').
options.notes: Mode 3 was added in v4.0 from SVT-AV1-PSY; v4.3.0 runs it on I-frames only in multi-threaded mode. Tune 3 forces mode 3.

options.description: Allows intra block copy (copying an already-coded area of the same frame), mainly useful for screen content.
options.notes: New in v4.2.0; still gated by --scm decisions and presets.

options.description: Enables film-grain synthesis: the encoder estimates a grain model and signals it so the decoder adds matching synthetic grain. The number sets how strongly grain is analyzed (and removed, with --film-grain-denoise 1).

effect.quality: keeps grain look; too high stacks noise or removes fine detail

recommendations.why: The project FAQ says about 8 suits live action with normal grain; Codec Wiki agrees.
Noisier video benefits from higher levels per the FAQ.
High-ISO sensor noise behaves like heavy grain for this purpose (FAQ treats CCD noise the same way).
Hand-drawn animation usually has little grain; about 4 works well.
Grainy (film-era) animation can use higher levels up to around 10.
If the 3D animation has no grain, leaving it off is faster and avoids losing fine detail.

options.lumora: Same level on both paths: EncodeRecipes.svtGrainLevel gives 12 for heavy grain, 8 for old anime, 4 for low light (8 for other kinds when forced on), used by the planner's 'grain' extra and by the encoders.json 'grain' tune through {svt_grain}. Offered on presets 6 and slower only, priced per rung from measured CPU time (+142% at preset 6 down to none at preset 1). Dropped when a measured --fgs-table is used (docs/encoding/tuning-svtav1.md).
options.notes: Above preset 6 the encoder warns of significant compute overhead (Lumora's ladder includes presets 8 and 10). Lumora's level for old anime (4) is lower than the FAQ's 'up to ~10' for grainy animation. --adaptive-film-grain (default on) adapts the synthesis block size to resolution.

options.values: 0: no denoising (grain params still sent), 1: denoise at the --film-grain level
options.description: Chooses whether the encoder also removes the grain from the picture it codes. With 0 it codes the original and only adds a grain description; with 1 it codes a denoised picture and relies on synthesis.

effect.quality: 0 keeps real detail; 1 can erase fine detail

recommendations.why: The FAQ says disabling source denoising can give higher fidelity if the level is checked by eye or high-fidelity metrics, warning that too high a level then stacks noise.
Codec Wiki recommends plain --film-grain without denoise in most cases because denoising always removes fine detail.
The FAQ says removing the grain and replacing it with synthetic grain is where the large efficiency gains come from.

options.lumora: Always 1, on the planner path and in the encoders.json grain tune: Lumora scores grain synthesis against a de-grained master, and denoise 0 cost 22-30% VMAF BD-rate on heavy grain while stacking synthetic grain on coded grain. Removed when --fgs-table is used; Lumora then denoises the frames itself (docs/encoding/tuning-svtav1.md).
options.notes: Default changed to 0 (from SVT-AV1-PSY). Ignored with a warning when --film-grain is 0. With --fgs-table the app disables encoder denoising.

options.values: path to a 'filmgrn1' text grain table
options.description: Supplies a pre-computed AV1 film-grain table instead of the encoder's own estimate. Format: a 'filmgrn1' line, then per time range 'E start end apply_grain seed update', and if update is 1 a 'p' line (ar_coeff_lag ar_coeff_shift grain_scale_shift scaling_shift chroma_scaling_from_luma overlap_flag cb_mult cb_luma_mult cb_offset cr_mult cr_luma_mult cr_offset), 'sY n x y...', 'sCb n ...', 'sCr n ...', then 'cY' with 2*lag*(lag+1) AR coefficients and 'cCb'/'cCr' with one more each. Times are 100 ns units from the first encoded frame; ranges include start, exclude end, and grain is off outside them.

effect.size: much smaller if the input is pre-denoised

recommendations.value: a table measured from the film, fed with a denoised input
recommendations.why: With a table the encoder does not denoise (the app turns --film-grain off), so the input must already be clean or grain doubles.

options.lumora: 'Grain measured from this film': '--fgs-table {grain_table}' written by GrainTable.write (one E entry 0..INT64_MAX, seed 7391, lag 0, scaling_shift 11, 10 luma points, no chroma). Lumora strips --film-grain/--film-grain-denoise and denoises the frames itself. That layout satisfies the v4.3.0 parser (seed <= 65535, lag <= 3, <= 14 luma points, one cCb/cCr coefficient at lag 0).
options.notes: v4.3.0 added timed tables (multiple time ranges) and per-picture grain via the API; earlier builds used the table more simply, so multi-entry tables may behave differently on older versions. Seeds advance per picture. Frame timing comes from --fps-num/--fps-denom, so raw input needs a correct rate. Same format as libaom's --film-grain-table.

options.description: Super-resolution: codes frames at reduced width and lets the decoder upscale them (1 fixed, 2 random, 3 by qindex threshold, 4 tries both and picks).
options.notes: Not supported in low delay.

options.description: Horizontal downscale factor (8/denom) for superres mode 1.
Superres downscale factor for key frames in mode 1.
Qindex threshold above which mode 3 starts downscaling frames (63 means never).
Key-frame threshold for superres mode 3.
Inserts switch frames (S-frames) at this interval so players can switch between streams at those points.
options.notes: Random-access S-frames since v3.1.0; rejected with all-intra in v4.3.0.

options.values: 1: only if alt-ref, 2: next alt-ref (default), 3: adjust mini-GOP for a given position, 4: position in decode order
options.description: How S-frame positions are chosen.
options.notes: Help prints range [1-3] but describes mode 4 (added v4.0).

options.description: Exact frames to make into S-frames for modes 3/4.
QP for inserted S-frames; one value applies to all.
options.notes: New in v4.0.

options.description: QP offset for inserted S-frames; one value applies to all.
options.notes: New in v4.0.

options.values: 0: none, 1: fixed scale, 2: random scale, 3: dynamic scale, 4: random access
options.description: Reference scaling: codes frames at a lower resolution in both directions (fixed, random, buffer-driven for CBR low delay, or event-driven).
options.notes: Docs default 0. Mode 3 only works in 1-pass CBR low delay.

options.description: Scale factor (8/denom) for resize mode 1.
options.notes: Docs default 8.

options.description: Key-frame scale factor for resize mode 1.
options.notes: Docs default 8.

options.description: Frames where resize mode 4 switches to new scale factors.
options.notes: All three event lists must have the same length.

options.description: Key-frame scale factors for each resize event.
Inter-frame scale factors for each resize event.
Requests lossless coding.

effect.speed: slower than lossy encodes (no verified figure)

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki's v3.0 tests found the output not bit-exact on most clips and often larger than x264 -qp 0.

options.notes: v3.1.1 and v4.3.0 contain lossless fixes, so the v3.0 finding may be outdated; not re-verified for v4.3.0.

options.description: Still-picture mode with optimizations and lower memory for single images (AVIF).
options.notes: Presets above 9 map to 9. v4.0 allows 2-3 frames for alpha layers.

options.values: 0-12, 22 (1 bt709, 2 unspecified, 9 bt2020, 12 smpte432 ...; names accepted)
options.description: Signals the color primaries of the content in the sequence header. Only a label: it does not convert pixels.

effect.quality: none (wrong value = wrong colors on playback)

recommendations.why: HDR10 and HLG use BT.2020/BT.2100 primaries, as in the official HDR example.

options.lumora: '--color-primaries {cp}': 1 for SDR, 9 for PQ and HLG targets.
options.notes: Default 2 means unspecified; players then guess, usually BT.709.

options.values: 0-22 (1 bt709, 13 srgb, 16 smpte2084/PQ, 18 hlg ...; names accepted)
options.description: Signals the transfer function (gamma, PQ or HLG). This is what tells players a stream is HDR.

recommendations.why: Listed values for PQ and HLG in the color appendix.

options.lumora: '--transfer-characteristics {tc}': 1 SDR, 16 HDR10, 18 HLG.
options.notes: In the svt-av1-hdr fork, 16 also switches variance boost to its PQ curve automatically; mainline has no such link.

options.description: Signals the RGB-to-YUV matrix used to make the input.

recommendations.why: Matches BT.2100 YCbCr used by HDR10/HLG.

options.lumora: '--matrix-coefficients {mc}': 1 SDR, 9 HDR.

options.description: Signals limited (16-235 style) or full range samples.
options.lumora: Always '--color-range 0' (studio).
options.notes: HDR10 deliverables are normally studio range.

options.description: Signals where 4:2:0 chroma samples sit relative to luma, so the decoder upsamples chroma correctly.

recommendations.why: The official HDR example uses topleft (colocated), the usual chroma siting for BT.2020 UHD masters.

options.notes: Parameters.md says FFmpeg does not pass this through, but current FFmpeg libsvtav1 code maps left and topleft chroma locations, so that note looks outdated. 'left' (vertical) is the usual SDR position. Lumora does not set it (unknown).

options.description: Writes SMPTE ST 2086 mastering-display metadata (display primaries, white point, peak and minimum luminance) into the AV1 stream for HDR10.

recommendations.why: Same syntax and coordinate set as the official example; luminance is given directly in nits.

options.lumora: '--mastering-display {svt_mastering}' on HDR10 exports only: HDRMetadata.svtMastering always writes P3-D65 primaries and L(peak nits as integer, min nits).
options.notes: Unlike x265, no 50000/10000 scaling. Out-of-range values are clipped. Lumora assumes a P3 mastering display for every HDR10 job, which is the common case but not universal.

options.description: Writes CTA-861.3 content light level metadata: brightest pixel (MaxCLL) and brightest frame average (MaxFALL) in nits.

recommendations.why: Format given in the color appendix; real values let displays tone-map well.

options.lumora: '--content-light {maxcll},{maxfall}' on HDR10 exports, from the measured or target metadata (0,0 when unknown).

options.description: Variance-based adaptive quantization: gives low-contrast superblocks (skies, skin, fog, night scenes) a lower qindex so they keep detail instead of collapsing into blocks.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki found the default strength beats no boost on nearly every clip and metric except VMAF.
The appendix targets night, foggy and overexposed scenes specifically.
Still helpful on flat areas, but only the svt-av1-hdr fork has a PQ-specific curve.

options.lumora: Optional 'Protect flat and dark areas': '--enable-variance-boost 1', plus '--variance-boost-curve 1' for low light and '--variance-boost-strength 1' for fast motion; turning it off cost 2-17% XPSNR BD-rate on every clip (docs/encoding/tuning-svtav1.md).
options.notes: Automatically disabled with CBR and with --aq-mode 1. Forced on by tunes 3 and 4. Default on in svt-av1-hdr.

options.description: How hard low-contrast superblocks are boosted (1 mild, 2 gentle, 3 medium, 4 aggressive).

effect.quality: + in flat areas as it rises

recommendations.why: Best for simple, untextured or smooth animation.
Broadly compatible; good for most live action and textured animation.
Detailed-texture animation fits the default curve.
Suited to content mixing very high- and low-contrast scenes such as horror or thrillers.
Codec Wiki suggests this pairing for more consistent gains at very high quality.

options.lumora: '--variance-boost-strength 1' with variance boost for fast motion only (ahead on VMAF, VMAF NEG and XPSNR on the action clip); the default (2) elsewhere, where 1 and 3 split VMAF and XPSNR (docs/encoding/tuning-svtav1.md).
options.notes: 4 prints an 'aggressive' warning and can inflate bitrate and make grain preservation inconsistent.

options.description: How much of a superblock must be low-contrast before it is boosted: 1 boosts if 1/8 is flat, 8 only if all of it is.

recommendations.why: Recommended range in the appendix; lower is less efficient, higher leaves low-quality holes.
Codec Wiki found octile 8 barely helps and can hurt.

options.notes: Codec Wiki's v3.0 article treats 6 as the default; the installed help says 5.

options.description: Selects the variance boost formula: 0 standard, 1 extends boosting to low-medium contrast areas at a modest bitrate cost, 2 tuned for still images (SSIMULACRA2 on CID22).

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki found curves 0-2 mostly indistinguishable, with curve 2 better on a few clips.

options.lumora: '--variance-boost-curve 1' with variance boost for low light only (ahead on VMAF, VMAF NEG and XPSNR there); default curve elsewhere (docs/encoding/tuning-svtav1.md).
options.notes: Curve 3 (PQ-optimized) exists only in svt-av1-hdr. Tunes 3 and 4 force curve 2.

options.description: Narrows the QP gap between temporal layers in a mini-GOP, so quality fluctuates less frame to frame at some cost in average efficiency.

recommendations.why: The psychovisual appendix says level 1 improves consistency at almost all quality levels at nearly no cost.
Higher levels help when maximum fidelity or very low CRF is the goal.

options.notes: The API header comment says default 1, but the v4.3.0 library default and help say 0.

options.description: Chooses the block size the grain model is estimated from based on resolution, which reduces visible repeating grain patterns.

recommendations.why: The appendix says it often greatly improves grain consistency.

options.notes: Made switchable in v4.0 (from SVT-AV1-PSY).

options.description: Largest transform allowed. AV1's 64-point transforms drop their top 32 frequencies, which can blur fine texture; 32 prevents that.

recommendations.value: 32 for still images or very high quality
recommendations.why: The appendix says it improves consistency especially for stills at medium-high quality; the encoder warns it may cost efficiency when QP >= 25.

options.notes: Tune 3 sets 32 when QP <= 45.

options.description: Psychovisual energy-preservation term: penalizes reconstructions that lose high-frequency 'energy' compared with the source, like x264/x265 psy-rd.

recommendations.why: Moderate values keep sharpness in textures and complex motion.
High values with TF and CDEF off can dramatically improve retention of real grain.

options.lumora: Optional 'Keep texture energy': '--ac-bias 1.0' for live action, CG, heavy grain and low light (smaller at equal VMAF and XPSNR on those clips; about +7% CPU time) (docs/encoding/tuning-svtav1.md).
options.notes: Added in v4.0 (from SVT-AV1-PSY). svt-av1-hdr's tune 6 bundles ac-bias 4.0 with fork-only options.

options.description: Bit depth of the mode-decision path for 10-bit encodes. Full 10-bit decisions are more accurate for gradients but slower.
options.notes: New in v4.2.0. Values 1 and 2 are rejected with 8-bit encoding. No published benchmark found; whether 1 reduces banding in HDR gradients is unverified.

recipes.name: Balanced archive, live action (SDR)
recipes.goal: Small file, transparent-looking quality, reasonable time
recipes.why: Preset 4 is the community balance point; variance boost, QMs and weaker temporal filtering each tested positive; long closed GOPs suit home playback. CRF is a starting point to adjust by eye or metric.

recipes.name: Maximum efficiency archive
recipes.goal: Smallest file when encode time does not matter
recipes.why: Preset 2 sits near preset 1 efficiency at half the time; QP-scale compression 1 adds consistency almost free.

recipes.name: Film with normal grain (synthesis)
recipes.goal: Keep the grain look without paying for it in bits
recipes.why: Level 8 is the project's live-action default; leaving denoise off keeps real detail when the level is verified.

recipes.name: Heavy grain, maximum savings
recipes.goal: Strongly reduce bitrate on very grainy or high-ISO sources
recipes.why: Noisier sources take levels 10-15; denoising the coded picture gives the big savings at some risk to fine detail.

recipes.name: Heavy grain, keep the real grain
recipes.goal: Preserve authentic grain instead of synthesizing it (bigger files)
recipes.why: The SVT-AV1 psychovisual appendix names this combination for dramatically better grain and noise retention.

recipes.name: Hand-drawn anime
recipes.goal: Clean lines and flat color at low bitrate
recipes.why: Low grain level and mild variance boost suit smooth animation; QMs helped the anime test set; +1 sharpness is in the safe range. Higher CRF than live action is fine per the FAQ.

recipes.name: Old film-era anime
recipes.why: Grainy animation can use levels up to about 10; turning TF off keeps more of the source grain; the animation deep dive found TF-off results clip dependent, so compare against --tf-strength 1.

recipes.name: Clean CGI / 3D animation
recipes.goal: Detail retention without needless grain processing
recipes.why: Grainless 3D animation should skip film grain (faster, no detail loss); default variance boost strength suits detailed textures.

recipes.name: Screen recording
recipes.why: Mode 1 forces palette and block-copy tools that make text and UI cheap to code.

recipes.name: HDR10 master
recipes.why: Full color description plus ST 2086 and CLL metadata in the documented syntax; luminance-qp-bias left off because it is not suited to PQ.

recipes.name: HLG broadcast-style HDR
recipes.why: HLG needs only the color description; Codec Wiki allows luminance bias on HLG (test 10-50).

recipes.name: Streaming rendition with a bitrate cap
recipes.goal: Quality-targeted encode that never exceeds the delivery ceiling
recipes.why: Capped CRF bounds peaks; short GOPs help seeking; tiles and fast-decode help weaker decoders.

recipes.name: Exact size (two-pass VBR)
recipes.why: Multi-pass matters most for VBR targeting.

recipes.name: Fast preview
recipes.why: Preset 8 is the fastest preset Codec Wiki still considers usable; 9+ shows inconsistent quality.

recipes.name: Still image (AVIF payload)
recipes.why: IQ tune is designed for still images and sets QMs, sharpness, variance boost curve 2 and transform limits itself.

forkAndVersionNotes.summary: Only the installed mainline v4.3.0 options are documented above. Options that look familiar from guides may belong to forks or other versions.
newInMainline: v4.3.0: timed --fgs-table entries; experimental --fast-decode 3 (special build only, not in this help)

v4.0.0: --tune 3 (IQ), --max-tx-size, --adaptive-film-grain, --ac-bias, --scm 3, extended CRF to 70 in 0.25 steps, --sframe-qp/--sframe-qp-offset, --sframe-mode 4 (all ported from SVT-AV1-PSY where noted)
v3.1.0: --chroma-qm-min/--chroma-qm-max, --rtc, random-access S-frames, variance boost refinements
v2.3.0/v3.0.0: --lp redefined as level of parallelism; preset renumbering
forkOnlyNotInInstalledBuild: SVT-AV1-PSY (archived 2025): its tune 3 was 'subjective SSIM', not mainline IQ; most of its features were merged into mainline 3.x/4.x
Successor: the PSY README points to svt-av1-hdr, while the Codec Wiki PSY page names svt-av1-psyex; the two sources disagree
helpVsDocsDisagreements: --hierarchical-levels and --pred-struct: docs list extra values (0-1, all-intra) not in the help
--qp-scale-compress-strength: API comment says default 1, help and library say 0
--variance-octile default: help 5, Codec Wiki v3.0 article 6
--svtav1-params: help says keys follow config-file option names; Parameters.md and the parser use CLI names without '--'
--recode-loop: help lists only 0 and 4; Parameters.md documents levels 0-4 with default 4

lumoraFindings: Tuning results (docs/encoding/tuning-svtav1.md, SVT-AV1 v4.3.0 on an M3 Max): every finding below was measured with BD-rates on VMAF, VMAF NEG and XPSNR plus CAMBI, scoring grain synthesis against a de-grained master as Lumora does.
--lp is now a level derived from each instance's share of the cores (EncodeRecipes.svtParallelism), no longer the core count that the encoder clamped to 6.
--luminance-qp-bias is dropped for HDR10 (PQ) exports and --qm-min is raised to at least 8 there (EncodeRecipes.svtArgs).

Grain synthesis uses one level per content type on both paths (heavy grain 12, old anime 8, low light 4) with --film-grain-denoise 1, and is offered on presets 6 and slower only, priced per rung from measured CPU time.
With grain synthesis the temporal filter stays on (--tf-strength 1): 15-46% smaller than --enable-tf 0 against the noise-free original.

Per content type: --qm-min 6 for live action and old anime, 8 for anime, CG and low light; --ac-bias 1.0 for live action, CG, heavy grain and low light; --tune 0 for anime; --variance-boost-curve 1 for low light; --variance-boost-strength 1 for fast motion.
The --lookahead 120 extra produced bit-identical output and was removed; preset 10 was dropped from the ladder in favor of preset 9.
GrainTable.write output (filmgrn1, one entry, lag 0, seed 7391) matches the v4.3.0 parser rules.
